about_description: TogoTV by DBCLS is a portal site for video manuals, lecture videos, illustrations and training materials for useful databases (DBs) and web tools in the life sciences. As life science research has grown in both scale and diversity, the usage of databases and web tools has become more complex and specialized. The usage of databases and web tools is indispensable for the efficient progress of research, and the skill to use them is one of the essential factors for a researcher to learn. TogoTV creates and organizes a variety of information to help researchers, technologists, and beginners who want to use them to reach and further their research resources.

request_description: This form is to freely request useful databases and web tools, whether you recommend them or not, that you think should be introduced (or content updated) on 'TogoTV' provided by the  DBCLS. In addition to the video manuals, you can also request useful images here. As a general rule, we do not share your information with anyone. If there is no information or content you want on TogoTV, you can provide your own feedback and contribution to our service.

ht_intro: Heritage Trees is a project of the Kyoto Botanical Gardens — the oldest public botanical garden in Japan — marking its 100th anniversary by highlighting the remarkable trees growing in its grounds. In collaboration with the Gardens, TogoTV is systematically illustrating 38 trees that embody the history of botany in Japan, and releasing them as a resource for education, research and conservation.
ht_more_info: For more about Heritage Trees, see the {site}.
ht_hint: ▶ Click a season block at the bottom right to see that season's illustrations
ht_collab_label: Kyoto Botanical Gardens × Togo Picture Gallery
ht_why_slide_alt: Heritage Trees × TogoTV: record of the illustration and review process
ht_why_caption_1: No. 1 Flowering dogwood (spring): the illustration process
ht_why_caption_2: No. 6 Chinese witch hazel (spring): the illustration process
ht_why_caption_3: No. 14 Chinese fringe flower (spring): the illustration process
ht_why_p1: To broaden its botanical content, TogoTV is producing plant illustrations grounded in scientific observation, in collaboration with the Kyoto Botanical Gardens.
ht_why_p2: A scientific illustration of a plant has to be more than beautiful: it must capture morphology and diagnostic features accurately, which makes expert verification essential. TogoTV therefore looked for a partner who could provide review by plant specialists.
ht_why_p3: The Heritage Trees of the Kyoto Botanical Gardens include trees that are important in the history of Japanese botany as well as trees connected to a wide range of research. After discussion between the staff of the Gardens and of TogoTV, the Heritage Trees collaboration was chosen as the project best suited to botanical illustration and to being documented systematically.
ht_why_p4: Every illustration released here was produced through close discussion with the illustrator and reviewed by the tree doctors of the Kyoto Botanical Gardens. The slideshow on the left documents one such process: photographing a plant sample provided by the Gardens, examining its details under a stereo microscope, drawing the illustration, and reviewing the result.
ht_why_p5: AI image generation attracts a great deal of attention today, but for scientific illustration it remains essential to draw from the actual specimen, to examine it closely with instruments such as microscopes, and to reflect accurate information under expert review.
ht_why_p6: AI is good at schematic diagrams and mash-up imagery, but it falls short when the characteristics of an individual specimen have to be represented.
ht_why_p7: TogoTV will continue to expand its botanical content while keeping this scientific perspective at its centre.
dbcls_page_description: Videos explaining how to use the databases and tools provided by DBCLS
dbcls_intro_1: DBCLS carries out research and development on the integration of databases in Japan and abroad, and on applications and underlying technologies that make databases easier to use. It also supports the integration of data and existing databases, and develops the data standards needed for that. This work is carried out in collaboration with many related research institutions in Japan and overseas.
dbcls_intro_2: This page collects videos explaining how to use the databases and tools provided by DBCLS — from ways to make use of resources in your research through to the concepts behind their development.

outcome_report_text: This is a form for reporting how you have used TogoTV.
